title: Stability Experimentation Field Expedition (90-day): Steady-State Contingency & Micro-SLOs
summary: A 90-day cross-functional field expedition to validate steady-state reliability controls, experiment with micro-SLO bundles, and codify contingency behaviors for graceful degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
objective_list: Define a minimal micro-SLO taxonomy aligned to product-critical routes and model classes
Run three controlled degradation experiments to verify fallback and routing policies
Validate observability coverage (traces, token-level latency, prefix cache hit-rate) for SLO signal fidelity
Create automated runbooks and a one-click rollback path for common degradation modes
Deliver an ops playbook and migration checklist for feature teams to adopt micro-SLOs
scope: Focus on three product routes (chat-generation, embedding, long-sequence batch inference), two model classes (lightweight quantized and high-fidelity full-precision), and the cross-cutting observability pipelines; exclude new hardware procurement and billing model changes.
roles_and_responsibilities: Priya Nair — SRE lead: expedition owner, timeline owner, exec communications
Owen Patel — Observability: metrics/tracing dashboards, alert tuning
Marissa Chen — Serving-runtime engineering: traffic-split policies, KV cache instrumentation
Diego Alvarez — Platform engineering: routing policy enforcement, capacity reservations
Lina Gomez — Product-hosted-api PM: stakeholder liaison, route prioritization
Ethan Brooks — Solutions engineering: customer impact simulation, canary customers
high_level_timeline: Week 1-2: design and hypothesis framing; Week 3-6: instrumentation and small-scale experiments; Week 7-10: canary degradations and rollback hardening; Week 11-12: documentation, training, and handoff
milestones: M1: Micro-SLO taxonomy and signal map (end of week 2)
M2: Observability gaps closed for token-latency and cache-hit signals (end of week 5)
M3: First controlled graceful-degradation experiment completed with rollback (end of week 8)
M4: Ops playbook and runbooks published; 2 feature teams onboarded (end of week 12)
experiments: Exp-A: Prefix-cache cold-start simulation — impact on median and p99 token latency
Exp-B: Model-variant fallback under load — route 10% traffic to quantized model for 20 minutes
Exp-C: Regional capacity stress with smart-routing fallback — failover from primary region to secondary with preserved SLOs
monitoring_and_alerting_plan: Add token-level latency histograms, prefix cache hit-rate and TTL metrics, model-variant error breakdown. Create SLO burn-rate alerts and a short-form degradation alert channel with playbook links. Configure synthetic probes against the three product routes with noise-injection capability.
rollback_and_contingency_criteria: Auto-rollback if p99 token latency increases > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes
Fallback to previous model variant if semantic-quality evals drop > 5% on canary prompt set
Abort cross-region failover if client-side error rate increases > 1% absolute
communication_plan: Weekly expedition status note (email + #sre-experiments Slack). Real-time incident channel for experiment windows. Exec summary at midpoint and final readout with metrics, learned heuristics, and recommended guardrails.
risk_register: Quality regression when routing to quantized models — mitigated by small canary slices and evals
Insufficient observability signal for prefix-cache behavior — mitigated by targeted instrumentation sprint
Customer-facing latency spikes during experiment windows — mitigated by throttled traffic and pre-notice to key customers
open_questions: What is the minimal set of prompts for meaningful semantic-quality evals across customers?
Which feature teams are willing to accept a 10-minute window for controlled degradations during business-hours?
Do existing RBAC and runbook approvals support one-click rollback for Dedicated customers?
acceptance_criteria: SLO signal coverage >= 90% for target routes
At least one successful graceful-degradation experiment produced a verified rollback and updated runbook
Two feature teams have integrated the micro-SLO checklist into their release gates
next_steps: Schedule kickoff workshop w/ stakeholders (week of 2026-02-02), create instrumentation tickets (JIRA-SRE-3421, JIRA-SRE-3499), reserve a canary window with two low-risk customers, and allocate 2 engineers for the first 4 weeks to close observability gaps.
